Shared growth is not felt by customers alone. It is felt by employees who grow as the Company grows, by distributors whose livelihoods are built on the same trust they help create, by partners and vendors who are part of an ecosystem grounded in doing things right and by shareholders whose long-term conviction is honoured every time SBI Life chooses lasting value over short-term gain. When growth is rooted in trust, it does not belong to one stakeholder. It belongs to all of them.

Built on Trust. Shared in Growth.
For over 25 years, SBI Life has helped individuals and families ascend in life’s milestones with confidence, preparedness and financial security. This trust has been earned through products that respond to actual requirements, service that brings clarity, claims support that stands by customers when it matters most and relationships built with care and responsibility. As protection needs evolve, the Company continues to strengthen its role as a dependable life insurer, enabling people to plan for tomorrow with assurance.
Growth that is shared is the only kind worth building.
The next 25 years will be defined by reach, how far the Company goes, how deep it penetrates into underserved India, how many more families are brought under the shelter of meaningful Insurance cover. The foundation for that journey has been laid, trusted relationship for life time. And it will carry SBI Life forward, into every corner of a growing, aspiring, unstoppable India.

India’s growth is being shaped by millions of aspirations. For a first-generation earner in a smaller town, protection can help convert a new income into lasting security. For an entrepreneur, it can support continuity beyond the uncertainties of business. For a retiree, it can bring dignity, stability and peace of mind. Their journeys may differ, but the need remains shared: the confidence to protect what they value and participate in growth with greater certainty.
Our Purpose
SBI Life’s purpose lies in widening this assurance across geographies, income groups and life stages, making the promise of protection more accessible to a changing India.

TREND #3
Regulatory Reform is Reshaping the Industry's Architecture
India's Momentum and the Opportunity It Creates
Context
SBI Life's response

SBI Life's response
FY26 marked one of the most active regulatory periods in the recent history of Indian life insurance. The IRDAI's overarching vision of Insurance for All by 2047 continues to drive structural reforms across the sector. The GST exemption on individual life insurance premiums, introduced in September 2026, is widely regarded as one of the most meaningful demand stimulants the industry has received in years, improving affordability and expanding access for households across income levels. Alongside this, the FDI limit was raised to 100%, the free-look period was extended from 15 to 30 days. The announcement of a transition to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) from April 1, 2027 will further align India's insurance reporting with global standards, enhancing transparency and investor confidence.

SBI Life welcomed the GST reform and, in keeping with its customer-first philosophy, passed the full benefit of the exemption to its customers without exception, absorbing the input tax credit transition internally. The Company has sought one-year forbearance to enable a controlled, regulator‑aligned transition to Ind AS with timely execution of the Board‑approved action plan. The Company remains committed to achieving full Ind AS compliance within the proposed timeline under strong governance and Audit Committee oversight. The Company's 13th month persistency improved and its mis-selling ratio remains lowest amongst private players, reflecting a governance posture that is consistently ahead of regulatory expectations.
India enters FY26 as one of the most compelling growth stories in the world and for the life insurance sector, with favourable environment. A fast-growing economy, a young and aspirational population, a reform-oriented regulator and a vast underinsured market together create a structural opportunity that will define the next decade of growth for this industry. SBI Life is not simply a beneficiary of this environment. It is an active participant in shaping it, deepening distribution, broadening product access and building the financial resilience of millions of Indian families.

TREND #4
Digital Technology is Redefining How Insurance is Experienced
TREND #1
A Growing Economy Creates a Growing Need for Insurance
Context
SBI Life's response
The digitisation of insurance is accelerating across every dimension, from distribution and onboarding to underwriting, servicing and claims. The online channel is growing rapidly, where customers are increasingly researching, comparing and purchasing independently. Artificial intelligence and machine learning are transforming risk assessment, pricing and customer engagement. At the same time, rising cyber threats and data privacy risks are creating new governance imperatives for insurers. The life insurance industry's digital transformation is no longer a strategic choice; it is an operational necessity.

In FY26, 99.7% of SBI Life's individual proposals were submitted digitally and processed through automated underwriting. The online channel grew 46.8% on APE basis during the year. The Company's revamped RIA chatbot, enhanced with GenAI capability, serves over 66,000 users every month. Deep integration with SBI's YONO ecosystem and SBI Life's Smart Care self-servicing app provide a seamless, frictionless experience at scale. On cyber and data governance, the Company holds ISO 27001:2022 certification, maintains a Security Operations Centre and has a Board-approved Data Governance Policy, ensuring that its digital ambition is matched by institutional responsibility.
Context
SBI Life's response

SBI Life's response
India's real GDP grew by 7.7%, firmly establishing the country as the fastest-growing major economy in the world. The RBI implemented three repo rate cuts in FY26, lowering the policy repo rate from 6.25% to 5.25%, a 100 bps reduction during FY26 and 125 bps cumulatively since February 2025, stimulating household consumption and financial confidence. India is projected to add 140 million middle-income households by 2030, with 68% of the population in the working-age bracket. Rising incomes, formalisation of the economy and deepening financial awareness are together creating a continuous wave of first-time insurance buyers entering the system. According to Swiss Re, India's life insurance sector is projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.8% in real terms between 2026 and 2030, among the highest growth trajectories of any major market globally.

SBI Life crossed ₹ 1 lakh crore in Gross Written Premium for the first time in FY26, reaching ₹ 1,012.9 billion, a growth of 19.2%. Renewal premium grew 18.9% to ₹ 587.3 billion, reflecting the deepening trust of an expanding policyholder base. The Company's 5-year New Business Premium CAGR stands at 15.6%, consistently outpacing industry growth. SBI Life's private market share in Individual Rated Premium improved to 22.9% in FY26 and its total market share rose to 16.5%, evidence of sustained, broad-based growth in a rising market.
TREND #5
Demographics are Creating a Long-Term Structural Tailwind
TREND #2
Context
SBI Life's response
Customers are Asking for More Than Just a Policy
India is one of the youngest large economies in the world, with a median age of 28 years and 68% of its population in the working-age bracket. This demographic profile creates a natural, sustained pipeline of first-time earners, first-time borrowers and first-time insurance buyers entering the formal financial system. Simultaneously, India's ageing population, projected to grow from 10.5% of the population in 2022 to 20.8% by 2050, is creating rapidly expanding demand for annuity and retirement solutions. Rising life expectancy and improving awareness are beginning to close this gap.

SBI Life's annuity and pension business grew 34.1% in FY26 to ₹ 70.3 billion, reflecting the early stages of what the Company expects to be a structurally growing opportunity. Group savings, covering gratuity, superannuation and employee benefit solutions, surged 55.3% to ₹ 84.8 billion. The Company has expanded its agency network into Tier 3, Tier 4 and rural markets, adding 1,20,000+ agents on gross level and opening 120 new branches during the year, to reach first-time insurance buyers where they live. Through PMJJBY, the Company currently protects 52.3 million lives and through micro insurance, an additional 4.7 million, ensuring that the demographic dividend translates into financial security for every segment of India's population.
Context
SBI Life's response
Indian customers are evolving rapidly in their relationship with financial security, buying insurance more deliberately, in higher amounts, for longer durations and with a clearer understanding of what insurance means. Life insurance penetration in India stands at approximately 2.7% of GDP against a global average of approximately 3%. The shift is visible across multiple dimensions, demand for pure protection surging, participating products gaining traction, retirement planning becoming a priority and riders being attached at significantly higher rates.

While ULIP grew at 7.9%, SBI Life's participating segment grew 121.1% in new business premium in FY26. Individual pure protection grew 89.3% (NBP basis), the clearest indication of shifting customer intent. Annuity new business grew 34.1% to ₹ 70.3 billion, driven by growing retirement planning awareness. Individual sum assured grew 61.2% year-on-year, with rider sum assured now accounting for 31.5% of individual sum assured. The Company launched new products during the year – Smart Shield Plus, Smart Money Back Plus, Smart Platina Advantage, Money Back Saver and Group Pension Plus, taking its portfolio to 26 individual and 9 group products across every life stage.

B) Indian Financial Market & Household Savings Outlook India’s financial markets are strengthening, underpinned by moderating inflation, easing interest rates and increasing household participation in financial assets. Inflation has moderated, with CPI falling from 6.7% in FY22 to average 4.6% in FY25 and projected near the 4% target in FY27. Correspondingly, the RBI reduced the policy repo rate by a cumulative 125 basis points during 2025, from 6.50% at the start of the year to 5.25% by December 2025, supporting investment, consumption and household financial planning.
World Life Insurance Market
Global life insurance premium growth is expected to re-accelerate after a moderation in 2025 as the interest rate-driven surge witnessed during 2023–2024 normalises. According to Swiss Re, global life premiums are projected to grow at an average CAGR of around 2.5% in real terms during 2026–2027, compared with an estimated 2.2% in 2025.
Macroeconomic Environment
Emerging markets continue to show relatively stronger growth supported by domestic consumption, infrastructure investment and policy reforms, though they remain sensitive to global financial conditions such as capital flow volatility, currency movements and changes in global liquidity.

Overview of the Global Economic Environment and Key Trends Influencing Financial Markets
Emerging markets are expected to outpace advanced economies, with premium growth projected at around 3.8% CAGR during 2026–2027, supported by rising incomes, improving financial inclusion and the continued expansion of bancassurance distribution. Demand in these markets continues to be driven by risk protection and savings-linked products.
A) Global Economic Growth Outlook According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), global economic growth is expected to remain stable but below long-term historical averages. Global output is projected to grow at around ~3.3% over the next two years.
Household savings are increasingly shifting from traditional instruments to market-linked products, reflected in the rapid expansion of the mutual fund industry, whose AUM grew from USD 425.9 billion in FY21 to USD 864.0 billion in FY26 and is projected to reach USD 1.2 trillion by 2030. This trend supports growth in Unit Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs), offering both investment and protection benefits.

At the same time, structural trends including digital transformation and artificial intelligence are influencing global investment patterns. Nevertheless, risks such as geopolitical tensions, energy price volatility, trade fragmentation and rising global debt levels may continue to affect market sentiment.
In advanced markets, life premium growth is expected to remain steady at around 2.1% annually during 2026–2027, compared with a modest CAGR of 0.8% during 2020– 2024. Regional growth is projected at approximately 1.6% for North America, 2.4% for Western Europe and around 2% for advanced Asia-Pacific markets. In emerging Asia, savings premium growth in China is expected to moderate following strong expansion during 2023– 2025. However, excluding China, emerging markets are expected to maintain healthy momentum, with premiums projected to grow at around 3.9% annually, supported by steady demand and expanding retail distribution.
Growth in advanced economies is expected to remain modest at approximately 1.5%, reflecting slower productivity growth and tighter financial conditions. In contrast, emerging and developing economies are projected to grow at over 4%, supported by stronger domestic demand, favourable demographics and structural reforms.

At the same time, India’s credit environment remains supportive, with bank credit expected to be around 12–13% in FY26, enabling broader household access to formal financial products. The NBFC sector is also expanding rapidly, with AUM projected at ` 50 lakh crore by FY27, improving financial inclusion in semi-urban and rural areas. Structural shifts in banking deposits, including moderation in the CASA ratio, further reflect evolving household savings behaviour and deeper financial penetration.

However, core inflation in some advanced economies remains above central bank targets due to persistent services inflation and energy price volatility.

Segment-wise business performance
The life insurance sector can be broadly categorised into three product segments: participating, non-linked and unit-linked products. Non-linked products include traditional products that provide savings with protection benefits or purely savings or protection products. Non-linked products are further classified into participating products – that offer variable returns linked to the insurer’s performance – and non-participating products that provide fixed benefits. Unit-linked products (ULIPs) offer returns, directly tied to the performance of underlying debt and equity market investments.

How/Why a risk? 1. Impact on Long-Term Profitability and Cost Efficiency Lower policy persistency reduces renewal premium inflows, which adversely affects long-term profitability. Although SBI Life maintains healthy persistency levels (around 85–87% in the 13th month and 58–60% in the 61st month), sustaining policyholder retention remains critical for stable earnings. Participating life insurance products are savings-oriented protection plans where policyholders are entitled to a share in the surplus generated from the participating segment during the term of the policy contract. These products offer a guaranteed sum assured along with potential long-term returns through surplus distribution, if any, subject to the fund's performance. Policyholders receive at least a 90% share of the surplus, while the remaining is allocated to shareholders. The Company offers a range of participating insurance products designed to meet diverse customer needs, including whole life insurance that provides lifelong coverage, endowment life insurance products that provide benefits over a defined term and child plans that helps secure a child’s future financial needs through planned savings and protection benefits.

1 Brief outline on CSR Policy of the Company
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is about the way in which organizations meet their wider economic, social and environmental obligations towards all stakeholders and society at large. The Corporate Social Responsibility Policy of SBI Life Insurance has been designed in consonance with Companies Act, 2013 and the rules / directions made there under.
• The remuneration of all other employees shall be aggregate of Fixed Pay (including monetary and non-monetary perquisites) and Variable Pay. Revision in remuneration will be with approval of the Managing Director & CEO and governed by the HR policies of the Company.
SBI Life’s CSR Policy pertains to all activities undertaken by the Company towards fulfilling its Corporate Social Responsibility objectives. The Company primarily work towards the thematic areas of education, livelihood, healthcare and environment with the focus of delivering services/benefits predominantly to underprivileged sections of the society as far as possible. However, basis the requirements and needs of stakeholders, the Company may also undertake other CSR activities in lines with Schedule VII activities.

The Company’s CSR policy is reviewed by Corporate Social Responsibility Committee (CSRC) and approved by the Board of Directors. The Board discloses the contents of such Policy in its report and also places it on the Company’s website and also ensures that the activities are governed by CSR policy of the company. The CSRC, of the Board, as prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013 is responsible for over-seeing the Company’s CSR program, ensuring its compliance and reporting to the Board on a timely basis. The CSRC also formulates and recommends to the Board, an action plan on all CSR activities undertaken.
The annual CSR Budget would be approved by the Board on the recommendation of the CSR Committee, subject to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.

Yes. Information and cyber security are treated as strategic priorities that support operational resilience, business continuity, service excellence and long-term growth. Recognising the increasing dependence on digital infrastructure and information assets, the Company has integrated cyber and information security into its broader enterprise risk management framework.
All complaints are promptly acknowledged upon receipt, with resolutions delivered within the prescribed regulatory turnaround time of 14 days. Customers are provided with multiple channels to raise concerns, including the Company’s branch network, corporate website, mobile application and 24x7 toll-free contact center (via both voice and email)

The Company has established Board-approved Information and Cyber Security and Data Governance policies that define the principles, governance structures and minimum-security standards applicable across all business functions. These policies are available internally through the Company intranet, while the Privacy Policy is publicly accessible on the Company website through SBI Life Privacy Policy. In cases where regulatory or legal requirements prescribe stricter standards, those requirements are adopted to ensure adherence to the highest level of compliance.
Escalation Matrix: To facilitate efficient grievance resolution, the Company has implemented a structured four-tier escalation mechanism comprising:

2. Head Office – Head of Customer Service & Experience

Aligned with the guidelines issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, the Company’s security framework reflects strong oversight and commitment from senior management. The framework establishes clear accountability for the implementation, monitoring and enforcement of security controls throughout the organisation. It also promotes the responsible usage of technology systems and information assets while ensuring access is restricted to authorised users based on business requirements.

4. Internal Ombudsman, who serves as an independent authority for fair and impartial review of unresolved cases.

The scope of the Company’s security framework extends across customer information, intellectual property, business data and technology infrastructure. To strengthen protection against cyber threats, unauthorised access, data loss and manipulation, business units work closely with the Information Security Team to periodically assess risks and evaluate the evolving threat environment. Based on these assessments, suitable controls and mitigation measures are implemented to maintain the confidentiality, integrity and availability of critical information assets.
Customer Feedback: In addition to its grievance redressal system, the Company has established a structured approach to capturing customer feedback across all touchpoints. Such feedback is systematically reviewed, appropriate actions are undertaken and customers are kept informed of any resulting developments.

Additionally, the Company undertakes periodic customer surveys across different stages of the policy lifecycle to gather proactive insights. The results are systematically assessed and used to identify trends, refine processes and drive continuous enhancements in customer experience.
Further strengthening its governance practices, the Company has constituted a Data Governance Committee comprising senior representatives from key functions. The Committee periodically reviews governance initiatives and provides strategic guidance on data management and protection practices. Through a combination of organisational oversight and robust technical safeguards, the Company seeks to ensure responsible data stewardship, safeguard sensitive and personal information and maintain stakeholder confidence.

Assessment Methodology
For the current financial year, our focus remained on listed entities. To ensure consistency and comparability across evaluations, we developed standardized templates for extracting data from publicly available BRSR reports. FY 2025-26 disclosures were used wherever available while for others, the most recent available reports for FY 2024-25 were considered. These templates comprised 47 parameters, enabling a uniform approach to data collection across all value chain partners. Using the disclosures made in these BRSR reports, we conducted a comprehensive assessment to evaluate the ESG maturity of each partner, yielding valuable insights into the sustainability practices embedded within our value chain.

Key Findings of the Assessment
The assessment revealed significant variation in ESG disclosure levels across the nine BRSR Core attributes. Key highlights include:

• Lowest disclosure was recorded for Openness of Business (56.10%) and Embracing Circularity and Waste Management (68.64%), indicating these as key areas for improvement.

Meaning of internal financial controls with reference to Financial Statements

Meaning of internal financial controls with reference to Financial Statements
A company’s internal financial control with reference to financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial control with reference to financial statements includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.

39. Ind AS update International Accounting Standard Board (‘IASB’) has notified the amended IFRS 17, with global date of implementation starting from January 1, 2023. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (‘ICAI’) has issued exposure draft of amendments in Ind AS 117 on 8th February, 2022. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) vide its notification dated August 12, 2024 has notified the Ind AS 117 on Insurance Contracts. Further, on September 28, 2024, the MCA has issued a notification that insurance company may provide its financial statements as per Ind AS 104 for the purpose of consolidated financial statements till IRDAI notifies the Ind AS 117. The IRDAI (‘the Authority’) vide its communication dated July 14, 2022 on Ind AS implementation in Insurance Sector has conveyed its broad approach on Ind AS implementation and necessary steps to be initiated by the insurers. On 3 March 2026, IRDAI issued the Exposure Draft of the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, proposing mandatory adoption of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) by all insurers with effect from 1 April 2026. Thereafter, on 30 March 2026, IRDAI notified the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, mandating preparation and presentation of financial statements in accordance with applicable Ind AS, including Ind AS 117, with effect from 1 April 2026. The Regulations, inter alia, provide one year forbearance, at the discretion of IRDAI, for insurers facing implementation challenges, subject to submission of a Board approved Ind AS transition plan with defined milestones and quarterly submission of Ind AS financial information to IRDAI during the forbearance period.

On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020, and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (collectively, the “Labour Codes”). The Ministry of Labour & Employment published draft Central Rules and FAQs to enable assessment of the financial impact due to changes in regulations. The Company has evaluated the financial impact of the Labour Codes basis the FAQs of the Ministry of Labour & Employment and recognised incremental estimated liabilities towards employees’ past service benefits, determined based on actuarial valuation in accordance with AS 15 – Employee Benefits and guidance issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). The resulting incremental charge of ₹ 13,549 lakh has been recognised in the Revenue Account for the year ended March 31, 2026. The Company continues to monitor developments related to the Labour Codes and will assess any further impact on the measurement of employee benefits liabilities as and when they arise.

A life insurance policy where the policyholder is entitled to at least a ninety percent share of the surplus emerging in the participating fund and the remaining belongs to the shareholders.
Reinsurance claims
Claim amount received or receivable by the insurance company from a reinsurance company on occurrence of a reinsured event.
Net Premium

Net Premium
Every insurer is required to maintain an excess of the value of admissible assets over the amount of liabilities of not less than an amount prescribed by the IRDAI, which is referred to as a Required Solvency Margin. The actual excess of admissible assets over liabilities maintained by the insurer is termed as Available Solvency Margin.
The total premium written by the Company after deductions for reinsurance ceded.
Pension Business
Reinsurance premium ceded
Pension plans are offered by life insurance companies to help individuals build a retirement corpus. On maturity, this corpus is invested for generating a regular income stream, which is referred to as pension or annuity.
Net worth
Premium paid or payable by the insurance company to a reinsurance company in lieu of reinsurance protection.
Net worth represents the shareholders’ funds and is computed as sum of share capital and reserves including share premium share application money and fair value change account net of debit balance in profit and loss account.
Sum assured
Renewal premium
Persistency ratio
An absolute amount of benefit which is guaranteed to become payable on death/ maturity of the policy in accordance with the terms and conditions of the policy.
Life insurance premiums falling due in the years subsequent to the first year of the policy.

Life insurance premiums falling due in the years subsequent to the first year of the policy.
The ratio of life insurance policies remaining in force to all policies issued in a fixed period. Persistency can be measured in terms of number of policies or in terms of premium.
New Business Annualized Premium Equivalent (APE)
Return on Equity
Surplus
The ratio of profit after tax to average net worth for the period.
The sum of annualized first year premiums on regular premium policies, and ten percent of single premiums, written by the Company during the fiscal year from both retail and group customers.
The excess of the value placed on a life insurance company’s assets over the value placed on its liabilities.
Policy Lapse
Reversionary bonus
A life insurance contract lapses if the policyholder does not pay premium within the grace period as prescribed under the applicable regulations.
Surrenders
Reversionary bonus is expressed as a percentage of basic sum assured. Simple reversionary bonuses once vested become guaranteed.
The termination of a life insurance policy at the request of the policyholder after which the policyholder receives the cash surrenders value, if any, of the contract.
New Business Premium
Insurance premium that is due in the first policy year of a life insurance contract or a single lump sum payment from the policyholder.
Policy Liabilities

Policy Liabilities
The policy liabilities under an insurance contract are the benefits an insurance company has contractually agreed to pay to the policyholders, plus its future expenses less future premiums.
Rider
Surrender Ratio
The add-on benefits which are in addition to the benefits under a basic policy.
Total surrender divided by the average AuM of policyholders during the year.
New Business Regular Premium or Regular Premium
Risk reinsured
Insurance premium that is due in the first policy year of a life insurance contract excluding single premium.
POSP
Survival Benefit
The proportion of risk underwritten by an insurance company which it transfers to a reinsurance company for which a stated risk premium would be paid.
POSP-Point of Sales Person – Life Insurance means an individual who possesses the minimum qualifications, has undergone training and passed the examination as specified in the IRDAI Master Circular on Point of Sales Products and Persons – Life Insurance and solicits and markets only such products as specified by the Authority.
The amount of benefit which is payable at specific interval, on survival to that period during the period of contract as specified in the policy document. This is stated at the inception of the contract.
Non Linked business

Non Linked business
Life or Health Insurance contracts other than unit linked business. Also called as Conventional / Traditional business.
Risk retained
The proportion of risk underwritten by an insurance company that is retained by an insurance company in its own books after ceding a portion of risk to the reinsurance company.
Terminal bonus
Bonus declared under the policy in the year when the policy results into a claim either by death, surrender or maturity.
Non Participating business
Premium
Policies without participation in profits, means policies which are not entitled to any share in surplus (profits) during the term of the policy. Examples include pure risk policies such as fixed annuities, term insurance, critical illness etc.
The consideration the policyholder will have to pay in order to secure the benefits offered by the insurance policy
Term Insurance
Rural sector
It is a contract to pay benefits on death of the life assured during the specified period.
Rural Sector” means such areas which are administered under Gram Panchayats
Private life insurers
All Indian life insurance companies other than the Life Insurance Corporation of India.

Integrated Annual Report 2025-26
Top-up premium
Unit Linked business/product

Unit Linked business/product
This is an additional amount of premium over and above the contractual basic premiums charged at the commencement of the contract.
A life insurance contract or health insurance contract under which benefits are wholly or partly to be determined by reference to the value of underlying assets or any approved index.
Total Cost Ratio
Value of New Business / VNB / VoNB
Operating expenses including commission, provision for doubtful debts and bad debts written off divided by Gross Written Premium.
VoNB is the present value of expected future earnings from new policies written during a specified period and it reflects the additional value to shareholders expected to be generated through the activity of writing new policies during a specified period.
Transfer to Shareholders’ Account
The amount of surplus transferred from Policyholders’ Account to Shareholders’ Account based on the recommendation by the Appointed Actuary.
Value of New Business Margin / VoNB Margin / Margin as a percentage of New Business Annualized Premium Equivalent
Underwriting
The process by which an insurance company determines whether or not and on what basis it will accept an application for insurance.
VoNB Margin is the ratio of VoNB to APE for a specified period and is a measure of the expected profitability of new business.
Unit-linked fund
Variable business/product

Variable business/product
A unit-linked fund pools together the premiums paid by policyholders and invests in a portfolio of assets to achieve the fund(s) objective. The price of each unit in a fund depends on how the investments in that fund perform.
Products where the benefits are partially or wholly dependent on the performance of an approved external index/ benchmark which is linked to the product.
Vested Bonus
Bonus already accrued, which is declared and attached to a policy. Once vested it becomes guaranteed.

chunks.section: Jul 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · The long-term outlook for the Indian life insurance industry remains
chunks.text:
The long-term outlook for the Indian life insurance industry remains
encouraging, supported by strong economic fundamentals, a favorable
regulatory environment and increasing digital adoption. Against this backdrop,
SBI Life continued its growth trajectory from FY 2026 into the first quarter of
FY 2027, delivering a 14% increase in Individual Rated Premium, supported
by a favorable shift in product mix.
All product segments recorded growth on an Individual Rated Premium basis
and all key distribution channels achieved double-digit expansion. The
increasing contribution from protection solutions and guaranteed non-par
saving products reflects evolving customer preferences and our strategic
focus.
Looking ahead, the company remains confident in the long-term growth
potential of the life insurance sector in India and its ability to navigate the
evolving landscape with a continued focus on profitable and sustainable
growth.

towards protection-oriented products. The exemption of GST on individual policies

reflecting sustained customer confidence and long-term value creation driven by
disciplined execution.

First of all, we welcome the government's recent GST reform aimed at improving the
affordability and accessibility of life insurance. This move underscores the critical role of life
insurance sector that it plays in providing financial security across diverse segments of society
and supports the sector's long-term sustainable growth. It is also in line with the government's
goal of insurance for all by 2047. However, the industry players are required to reassess and
realign the strategies in light of non-availability of input tax credit under individual business
segments.
We believe the industry players will comfortably navigate these changes and work on
implementation of various measures to handle the said impact. Adhering to the core principle of
customer-first approach of the company, the company has passed entire GST benefit to its
customers. Additionally, in September, we enhanced the benefit amount, the return rate in the
Platina series of our non-participating guaranteed products by passing on the benefit of the yield
curve to customers.
Q2 was a good quarter for the company, marked by a strategic shift in the product mix with

Q2 was a good quarter for the company, marked by a strategic shift in the product mix with
robust performance in both individual and group protection segments. During the quarter, we
introduced two new products, Smart Shield Plus, a protection product and Smart Money Back
Plus, a participating product, tailored to meet the evolving needs of the customers.
Notably, Smart Money Back Plus received a good response and more than 8,500 customers
opted for the product in less than 15 days of its launch. Also, Smart Shield Plus contributes 11%
of the total protection sum assured. This strong early performance underscores the product's
relevance and its wide acceptance amongst customers.
